question.problem: Consider the equation $\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3x}{2})=-\frac{1}{2}$ for ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$ If the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ are written in ascending order,  what is the numerical value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{3}?$
question.worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3x}{2} & ={120}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}, & \, & \, & \frac{3x}{2} & ={240}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving our two equations for $x$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x & ={240}^{∘}+n\cdot {720}^{∘} & \, & \, & 3x & ={480}^{∘}+n\cdot {720}^{∘} \\ x & =\frac{{240}^{∘}}{3}+\frac{n\cdot {720}^{∘}}{3} & \, & \, & x & =\frac{{480}^{∘}}{3}+\frac{n\cdot {720}^{∘}}{3} \\ x & ={80}^{∘}+n\cdot {240}^{∘} & \, & \, & x & ={160}^{∘}+n\cdot {240}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x={80}^{∘}$ and $x={160}^{∘}$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x={320}^{∘}$ and $x={400}^{∘}.$ We reject the solution ${400}^{∘}$ since it lies outside the domain of interest.

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$ So, the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ (written in ascending order) are

$$
x={80}^{∘},\,{160}^{∘},\,{320}^{∘}
$$

Finally, since ${x}_{1}={80}^{∘}$ and ${x}_{3}={320}^{∘},$ the numerical value of ${x}_{1}\text{ }+{x}_{3}$ is $80+320=400.$
